images.title: (a + b)² is more than a² + b²
images.purpose: Compares the full square (a + b)² with the two squares a² and b² alone, showing the two missing ab rectangles.
images.composition: A before and after comparison: the full square on the left and the same square with two gaps on the right. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Left panel: a square split into four parts: top left teal (#0072B2) square labelled 'a²', bottom right teal square labelled 'b²', and two reddish purple (#CC79A7) rectangles top right and bottom left, each labelled 'ab'. Label '(a + b)²' below the left panel. Right panel: the same outline with only the two teal squares filled; the two rectangle spaces are empty with dashed grey (#6B7280) outlines. Label 'a² + b²' below the right panel. Centred beneath both panels, the label '2ab more' in reddish purple. Exactly 2 teal squares in each panel and 2 filled rectangles only in the left panel.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², which is more than a² + b² by 2ab.
images.description: Compares the full square (a + b)² with the two squares a² and b² alone, showing the two missing ab rectangles.
images.context: (6x + 5)² = 36x² + 60x + 25; a = 5, b = −2: 9 < 29, so not always greater.

image_decisions.why: The empty gaps show exactly what a² + b² leaves out, the most common squaring error.
